## Lent presentations

Overview of the Lent presentations

## Sell people on talks?

## Target your presentation

&nbsp;

Like writing, presentations are purposeful **communication** to an audience


::::: {.columns}

:::: {.column}

::: {.fragment}

* Know the **purpose**

   + Communicating findings
   + Making an argument
   + Getting a job

:::

::::

:::: {.column}

::: {.fragment}

* Know the **audience**

   + Academics (conferences)
   + Policy actors (policy meetings)
   + Lay people (public meetings)

:::

::::

:::::

&nbsp;

::: {.fragment .center}

*Everything you present should **serve your purpose** and **your audience***

:::

## Good presentations

&nbsp;

After one, your audience...

* understands what was done
* remembers the key points
* feels their time was well spent

. . .


::: {.center}

*Good presentations rarely closely follow a paper...*

:::

. . .

::: {.center}

*... but a good presentation is a great foundation for a paper*

:::

# Structure


## Classic structure

* Say what you’re going to say
   * Motivate
   * Outline
* Say it
   * Provide necessary background
   * Analysis
* Say what you said
   * Repeat key points
   * Provide a resolution

. . .

::: {.center}
*This is reliable and safe but an be boring and inefficient*
:::


## Anything else

People like a bit of drama

::: {.center}
*This is usually more engaging but requires more thought*
:::






## Example

How would you present this?

# Style

## Presentation style

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column}
**Be yourself**

* Humor
   * Can win audiences
   * Not always appropriate
* Audience engagement
   * High risk/reward

:::

::: {.column}
**Or don't**

* Play a role
* Use a script

:::

::::

## Slides

A little attention to slides goes a long way



## 

* Humor
   * If you're funny, can keep people engaged
   * But risk not being taken seriously and hard to calibrate for many audiences and purposes
* Engagement
   * Can keep people more interested
   * Hard to predict and control
* Language
   * Even simpler/clearer than paper
   * Use jargon only when everyone will understand or you can define it
* Script or no script


## Preparation

* Whether scripted or not, run through multiple times and time it
* You are a performer

## Content

* Calibrate to time

* Introduction
   * Minimal logistics, e.g., who you are
   * Hook immediately

* Time is precious
   * Trim all fat
   * Q&A exists for a reason

* Don't fight your slides
   * Minimize words
      * Key points
      * Cues for you
   * Interact with images

## Visuals

* Don't display anything you don't want them to look at
* Visuals will compete for attention
* Either extremely simple or you walk people through it

## Rehearse

::::: {.columns}

:::: {.column width="40%"}

* Keep time
* Make note of:

   * Forgotten points
   * Awkwardness
   * Clarity issues

## Present

::::: {.columns}

:::: {.column width="40%"}

* Slow down
* Your nervousness rarely shows
* Look at audience
* Q&A:
   * Pay attention, breathe, answer concisely

::::

:::: {.column width="60%"}

::: {style='width="100%"'}

## Some example talks {.dark-slide background-color="#133844" background-image="img/logo-light.svg" background-size="auto 60px" background-position="right 15px bottom 15px"}

* [Life-course processes as cause and effect of macro-level changes in gun violence. *European Society of Criminology Annual Meeting 2025*](https://clanfear.github.io/ESC_2025/slides.html)
   * A dense 12 minute theoretical talk

* [Exposure to gun violence and gun carrying from childhood to age 40 over a 25-year era of change *NCGVR Webinar Series 2025*](https://www.ncgvr.org/events/gun-violence-prevention-webinar-series/community-firearm-violence-exposure-weapon-carrying.html)
   * A 10 minute empirical talk---read from a script!

* [The promise and perils of the sharing economy: The impact of Airbnb lettings on crime. *University of Cambridge Alumni Festival 2025*](https://clanfear.github.io/alumni-festival_2025-09-27/slides.html)
   * A 45-minute empirical talk for a diverse audience

* [Reassessing 'the effect ofthe Seattle police-free CHOP Zone on crime'. *European Society of Criminology Annual Meeting 2024*](https://clanfear.github.io/ESC_2024/piza-connealy_comment/slides.html)
   * A 12-minute critique of a published paper
